clue.text: Battle fast with poles to secure toilet

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for a quick tempo

indicators.note: securing something means gripping and holding it, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: the north and south poles, N and S
a pan is the bowl of a lavatory

explanation.surface: A soldier goes without food while using poles to fix a latrine in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like going without food, but it is the tempo marking for quick playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestonpans was a 1745 Jacobite victory near Edinburgh, so it names a historic military engagement.

clue.text: Humourless female wicked in school

indicators.note: something placed inside sits within an outer piece

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
standard abbreviation
both are slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A stern woman with a wicked streak is found at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' means evil on the surface but is youth slang for great; 'school' is the whale kind, not a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone po-faced wears a solemn, disapproving expression and sees no joke, which is being without humour.

clue.text: European singer's ruined punk's hair thus?

parts.note: standard abbreviation

indicators.note: what a singer produces is sound, so the word that follows is to be taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: ruined means wrecked, which is spoken like this spelling

explanation.surface: A continental vocalist complains that the spiky punk hairstyle has been spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a punk's spiked hair stands up.
explanation.definitionFit: Punk hair is gelled into spikes or a mohican that stands straight upright, so it is described as upright and stiff.

clue.text: Drive on motorway disturbing Terry's hamper

indicators.note: to disturb is to break into something, so a piece intrudes into the middle of another

parts.note: Tel is a British pet form of Terry
to ram is to drive forcefully
M as in M1 is the motorway abbreviation

explanation.surface: A road-safety warning: speeding along the motorway spoils Terry's picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' poses as a picnic basket but is the verb. Tel is a familiar British shortening of Terry, as in the footballing nickname 'El Tel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trammel is to restrict or impede freedom of movement, which is what hindering someone does.

clue.text: Recent issue of novel largely supported

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new
borne is the past participle of bear, to support

explanation.surface: A publisher's note: the latest edition of a novel was mostly well received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a publication, but it is offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for children or offspring, so a recently arrived baby is recent offspring.

clue.text: A treatment centre served up dearest veg

parts.note: taken as written
a spa is a place for health treatments

indicators.note: in a down clue, something brought up reads from the bottom upward, so the letters run backward

parts.note: sugar is an endearment, like darling

explanation.surface: A health retreat has dished up its most expensive vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dearest' reads as most costly, but it is a term of affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a green spear-shaped vegetable, so it is an example of veg, the casual shortening.

clue.text: Keep using credit in half of shops

indicators.note: placed inside, so one piece sits within the remains of the other
taking only half means the back three of the six letters are discarded

parts.note: shops are stores; only its first half is kept
buying on tick is buying on credit

explanation.surface: A shopper keeps paying on credit in some of the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit. 'Shops' is a noun to be swapped for a six-letter synonym before it is halved.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep to a plan or promise means to adhere to it faithfully, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Fine iron runs through all the best fabric

indicators.note: a thread running through cloth lies inside it, so these letters sit within the outer piece

parts.note: ta-ta is a British informal goodbye
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Quality ironing runs over the finest cloth of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the best' looks like praise for the fabric, but it is a parting phrase, like the chirpy British goodbye ta-ta.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven silk or synthetic cloth, so it is a type of textile.

clue.text: Tory so tense probing Blair?

parts.note: so and that both mean to such a degree, as in 'not that big'

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so one letter is pushed into the middle of a name

parts.note: Cherie Blair, wife of Tony; the question mark marks a Blair by example
grammar abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Conservative is so nervous about investigating the Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' makes you think of Tony, but it is his wife, a different Blair; the question mark admits the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thatcherite follows the policies of Margaret Thatcher, Conservative prime minister, so is one kind of Conservative.

clue.text: Joker keeps double parking in London area

indicators.note: to keep is to hold onto, so the outer piece holds the following letters

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit
P for parking, doubled
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prankster keeps parking on double lines in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to the definition but is part of what goes inside. Wapping is a riverside district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wapping is a district by the Thames in the East End, so it is a named part of the capital.

clue.text: Dracula overwhelmed by this urge means to impart bite

parts.note: vampires are repelled by garlic in legend
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Dracula is defeated by his own craving, the very thing that makes him bite.
explanation.walkthrough: The first piece is a cryptic hint rather than a synonym: vampire lore has garlic warding off Dracula. 'Bite' sounds like fangs, but it is pungent flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A garlic press crushes cloves to release sharp flavour into food, so it is a kitchen tool for adding pungency.

clue.text: Turned to regulars in casual clothing

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the letters read backward

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regular letters are taken at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone switches to wearing their usual relaxed clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casual clothing' looks like the definition, but 'casual' is the letter source and 'clothing' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neck scarf or cravat worn by men, so it is an article of neckwear.

clue.text: Film producer winning Oscars never unoccupied

indicators.note: to win something is to take it in, so the outer word gains letters inside

parts.note: a maker produces things
O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet, so two of them

indicators.note: an unoccupied word has had its inside emptied, leaving just its two ends

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A film producer who keeps winning Oscars is never short of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscars' tempts towards the Academy Awards, but each is the radio-alphabet code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonraker is the 1979 James Bond movie starring Roger Moore, so it is a specific motion picture.

clue.text: Will extra fish here in Boulogne end in creel?

parts.note: the cod is a fish
ici is French for here

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A French angler wonders whether there will be more fish in the basket at Boulogne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is not the future tense but a testament. Boulogne is a French port, so 'here' goes into French. A creel is a fishing basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplementary document amending or adding to a testament, so it is an addition to one.

clue.text: Tea with juicy fruit bypassing electronic blender?

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea

indicators.note: to bypass is to go round, so the outer word goes around a letter

parts.note: a juicy fruit
E as in e-mail is short for electronic

explanation.surface: Tea and fruit go into a kitchen blender, avoiding the electric one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blender' suggests a kitchen gadget, but it is something that blends into its surroundings; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon changes skin colour to match its background, so it merges invisibly with its environment.

clue.text: Minor gentry drinking retro cocktail

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the letters run in the opposite direction
the outer words swallow the answer the way a drinker takes in liquid

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Members of the lesser landed classes are sipping an old-fashioned mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor gentry' reads as the subject of the sentence, but it is just the container of the letters, which read backward.
explanation.definitionFit: A Negroni is an Italian mixed drink of gin, vermouth and Campari, so it is a classic aperitif.

clue.text: Bakery regular, say, defends north in plain language

indicators.note: a defender surrounds and shields what it protects, so the outer word holds a letter

parts.note: an éclair is a staple pastry; 'say' marks an example
compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A regular customer at the baker's speaks up for the north in simple words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bakery regular' suggests a loyal customer, but it is a product the bakery always stocks.
explanation.definitionFit: En clair is a French phrase used for messages sent uncoded, so it means in ordinary readable text.

clue.text: Forester initially rings Belgian site delivering tree

indicators.note: a ring encircles, so the outer letters go round the place name
a person's initials are the first letters of their names

parts.note: C. S. Forester, author of the Hornblower novels
Ypres is a town in Flanders, scene of First World War battles

explanation.surface: A woodsman circles a Belgian spot to deliver a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forester' seems to be a woodsman, but it is the novelist C. S. Forester, whose initials are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is a conifer, often tall and slim, so it is a familiar evergreen species of wood plant.

clue.text: One regrets losing Penny's record again

indicators.note: to lose something is to be without it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a repenter is a person who regrets
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Someone regrets losing Penny's old vinyl, which they then want to play again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' is a verb here, to log something, not a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to record it in a ledger, so doing it a second time is to log it anew.

clue.text: Light pan fills space

indicators.note: whatever fills something goes inside it

parts.note: a gap is a space
to pan a show is to slam it, criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A lightweight cooking pan fills up the space in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective about the pan, and 'pan' looks like cookware; both are misreadings.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas lamp burns coal gas to give illumination, so it is a type of lamp, an old-fashioned source of illumination.

clue.text: Bouncer from star cheers Glamorgan's opener up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a big name is a star
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: an opener is what comes first, so the first letter is kept

parts.note: Glamorgan is a Welsh county cricket club; its first letter

explanation.surface: A star cricketer opening for Glamorgan bowls a bouncer and the crowd cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bouncer is a short-pitched ball, but here it is the doorman. Glamorgan is a Welsh county cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateman controls entry at a gate, just as a nightclub doorman decides who is let inside.

clue.text: Train crosses no English city

indicators.note: to cross something is to straddle it, so the outer word spans the letters

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it
nah is casual for no
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A railway journey that does not pass through any English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is the verb, to point a weapon, not a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaheim is a Californian municipality near Los Angeles, home of Disneyland, so it is an urban centre.

clue.text: Perhaps saw monkey and other primates disrupting rented property

parts.note: a cheeky child is a little monkey or imp

indicators.note: to disrupt is to break into the middle of something, so letters are inserted

parts.note: a let is a property rented out
humans are primates too

explanation.surface: A monkey and other apes were maybe seen running riot in a rented house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' tempts as the past tense of see, but it is the cutting tool; 'Perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is one kind of tool, and implement is a general word for a tool or utensil.

clue.text: Love following game

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a game leg is a lame one

explanation.surface: Someone is passionate about following a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' suggests tennis zero, and 'game' suggests a sport; game here is the old word for crippled.
explanation.definitionFit: A flame, as in an old flame, is a sweetheart or romantic partner, so it can stand for a beloved.

clue.text: High-flier drained frascati and regularly demolished gnocchi

indicators.note: a drained word has its contents poured out, leaving only its two ends

parts.note: first and last letters

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of the pasta

explanation.surface: A big shot drank up the Italian white wine and wolfed down the gnocchi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' reads as a successful person, but it is a bird. Frascati is an Italian white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A finch is a small seed-eating songbird, so it is a winged creature that soars aloft.

clue.text: Sinner ahead of all other players? The ultimate achievement

parts.note: Eve ate the forbidden fruit in Genesis
the rest of the field

explanation.surface: A cheat gets ahead of the field and celebrates the greatest triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of' only places one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest, the world's highest peak, is used figuratively for the highest goal one can attain.

clue.text: Hand Geordie reduced sentence primarily for good behaviour

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the leading letters are taken

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A Newcastle worker got his prison term cut for behaving well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' feels like a deletion signal, but it is just one of two words whose first letters are taken. A Geordie is a Newcastle native.
explanation.definitionFit: Manners are polite conduct and social etiquette, so they amount to proper conduct towards others.

clue.text: Beige round actor's posh house

parts.note: sand is a beige colour
a ring is round
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A performer has a grand home painted in beige all around.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandringham is the British royal family's country estate in Norfolk, the grandest of posh houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandringham House is a royal residence in Norfolk owned by the monarch, so it is a stately home.
